chapters.title: The Five Shares and the Long Road to the Shaykh
warnings: fluency-08-part-01: output near-identical to base — copied, not re-voiced
editorial_queries: The boy's "three goods" appears to enumerate the imam's upheld case, a well-counseled trust, and a graced dead man, but the source phrasing blurs whether these are truly three distinct items or two.
comprehension_flags: A reader may not realize that "his own greater father," "the greater scholar," and "the Shaykh, the lord of the house" all appear to refer to the same senior figure the Master brings the boy to meet.

A reader may stumble on "his elder father" and "the father who had been the cause of his grace," which both refer to the departing Master (not the boy's biological father), and on the opaque line "at the outset there is room enough for you."
terminology_notes: zakat — the source uses "alms/zakat" for two distinct ideas (the general purifying due, and here a specific one-fifth given to a binding claimant, closer to khums); the rendering "zakat" should be standardized book-wide and the one-fifth usage checked against how earlier chapters name it.

Shaykh — the senior figure's title is rendered "Shaykh" here but described elsewhere as "the greater scholar"/"greater father"; one consistent handling of this figure's title should be fixed book-wide.
"the Master" and "the Shaykh" — keep them as two distinct persons throughout; they are not interchangeable and must never be conflated.

terminology_notes: God / Allah — the source names the deity as "God" through the earlier exchange and shifts to "Allah" from the "just one of Allah" turn onward; this rendering preserves each occurrence as given, but the divine name should be standardized one way book-wide.
